newsitem.title: FRANCE: French environment minister wants canal scrapped.
newsitem.headline: French environment minister wants canal scrapped.

text.p: France's new environment minister, Dominique Voynet, said on Thursday in her first policy statement she wanted a controversial Rhine-Rhone canal project scrapped and the route of a planned eastern high speed train line changed.

Voynet, leader of the environmentalist Greens party, made the comments at a handover ceremony with outgoing centre-right minister for regional development, Jean-Claude Gaudin, whose portfolio she is also taking.
"I will insist that we guarantee the final abandonment of the wide Rhine-Rhone canal project," Voynet said on the steps of the ministry.

She also said that while the planned TGV-East high speed rail line, due to link Paris to Strasbourg and eventually Munich and Vienna, was necessary, its route would be revised in consultation with protesting residents' associations.

"There will no longer be any question of deciding in a vacuum that an infrastructure project is in the public interest. The public interest must be determined in consultation, in dialogue with citizens," she said.

Voynet, 38, the youngest minister in Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's left-wing coalition cabinet, said it was important that for the first time regional development and the environment were tied together in a single ministry.

"This could prefigure a future big 'deparment of sustainable growth' which would ensure that henceforth the major territorial development projects are handled together with their human and environmental consequences and their implications for natural resources," she said.
Voynet arrived on foot for the handover, walking into the courtyard of her ministry behind her passengerless chauffeur-driven ministerial limousine.

She said better consultation with citizens about major transport and public works projects would avoid conflicts and protest campaigns, such as her party's own campaigns against a nuclear fast-breeder reactor and the Rhine-Rhone canal.
